checks: Every witness satisfies every row because the row normals expose their own points among all vertices. In row i, p_i is tight, and strict exposure in all other rows gives positive slacks. The full-dimensional hull Q lies in L.

A relative neighborhood of p_i in the row hyperplane is feasible, giving a face of dimension 3. A small outward displacement along n_i violates just that row, proving irredundancy. Distinct rows give distinct facets by the exclusive witnesses. At a relative-interior point of any facet an active row is constant throughout that facet and hence describes it.

For each integer x in the entire space, the compact convex source conv(Q∪{x})×{0} contains x and every root at its base. The frozen hull result gives one root in every parity and no other lattice point in Q. The recurrence therefore stays in this finite lattice projection and terminates by the accepted orbit lemma.

The terminal barycenter is equivalent to the displayed integer sum, using sum_{j<k} 2^j=2^k−1. If x differs from p_s, at least one digit differs from p_s; all summands have nonnegative n_s margin and that digit has strictly positive margin. Thus x violates row s. The case k=0 is already a root.

For an arbitrary real x outside L choose a violated row i. At r=(p_i−alpha x)/(1−alpha) the same row is strict inward, and finitely many other positive slacks persist for small alpha>0. A ball around r gives a ball of radius scaled by 1−alpha around the integer witness p_i inside conv(L∪{x}). This treats every proper convex enlargement, including ones not given by finitely many closed inequalities.
